cards.b: The area of land drained by a river and its tributaries.
High ground that separates one drainage basin from another.
Confluence: where two rivers meet. Tributary: a smaller river that joins a larger one.
The force of water pushing into cracks in the bed and banks, breaking the rock apart.
The river's load scrapes and wears away the bed and banks.
Load particles collide with each other and become smaller and rounder.
Traction (rolling), saltation (bouncing), suspension (carried in the flow), solution (dissolved).
When it loses energy: shallow water, slow flow, inside of bends, drought or at the mouth.
Hard rock over soft rock; soft rock eroded faster, forming overhang and plunge pool; it collapses and retreats upstream leaving a gorge.
Erosion on the outside bend makes a river cliff; deposition on the inside makes a slip-off slope.
Formed when a river cuts through a narrow meander neck in flood, and the old bend is sealed off by deposition.
A natural raised bank formed when floods deposit the coarsest material next to the channel.
Landform at a river mouth where the river deposits its load in a weak-current sea or lake and splits into distributaries.
The time between peak rainfall and peak river discharge on a hydrograph.
Hard: built structures such as dams and embankments. Soft: working with nature, e.g. afforestation, flood zoning, warnings.

short.q: Explain how a gorge is formed.
short.model: A waterfall undercuts hard rock above soft rock, which collapses so the waterfall retreats upstream. The retreat leaves a steep-sided gorge behind.
In a flood, the river slows as it spills over its banks and drops its heaviest material first, next to the channel. Repeated floods build up raised banks.
points: flooding and slowing water causes deposition
coarse material dropped next to channel builds up banks

short.q: Explain why deforestation can increase flooding.
short.model: Fewer trees mean less interception and less water taken up by roots. More rain runs quickly over the surface into rivers, raising peak discharge.

short.q: Explain one disadvantage of using embankments to control a river.
short.model: Embankments can fail in a very large flood, causing a sudden and destructive flood. They also speed water downstream, increasing flood risk elsewhere.

short.q: Describe how a river's characteristics change downstream.
short.model: Channel width, depth and discharge increase while gradient falls. Load becomes smaller and more rounded.
points: load smaller and more rounded / gradient decreases
